newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks open firmer despite property fears, Dow weakness.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks open firmer despite property fears, Dow weakness.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks opened firmer on Friday despite Wall Street's overnight fall and continued property fears, and investors were switching into blue chips and speculating on red chips, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index was up 60.32 points at 12,419.02 after the first 29 minutes of trade. Turnover was HK$1.9 billion.
"There was no particularly exciting news overnight," said Sean Li, associate director Amsteel Securities.
Brokers said investors were switching into blue chips like HSBC Holdings Plc and still speculating on red chips and H-shares.
Brokers expected continued range-trading in the absence of data giving clues to the direction of U.S. interest rates and to the Dow industrials, which fell 23.79 to 6,540.05 overnight.
"I think short-term the (Hong Kong) market will be trading from 12,000 to 12,600," said Michael Ng, dealing director with Sassoon Securities.
Brokers said investors were also buying China Light and Power Co Ltd as a defensive strategy until they were more sure of medium-term trends in the market.
China-related red chips were bought on optimism they would have access to mainland asset injections, they said.

"Most of the negative news has been discounted. Everybody knows the property market is going to consolidate or face and adjustment of five to 10 percent," said a sales representative with a European house.
He said property stocks had found a floor after selling earlier in the week, and some had bought back their own stock.
HSBC was up HK$1.50 at HK$182.5, and shares in China Light were up HK$0.70 at HK$35.20, also buoyed by news it was in a Shenzhen power plant joint venture with a unit of Exxon Corp.
Shares in Shanghai Industrial, which said on Wednesday it was placing new shares and would pay US$600 million for a stake in two Shanghai roads, were up HK$0.60 at HK$36.40.
Fellow red-chip CITIC Pacific was up HK$0.30 to HK$38.00, and China Resources was up HK$0.45 at HK$17.80.
Among property stocks, Henderson Land lost HK$0.25 to HK$63.75, but Sun Hung Kai Prop was up HK$0.25 at HK$76.75 and New World was flat at HK$40.30.
